table.brief: A/B test results: Metric / Control (mean, 95% CI) / Variant (mean, 95% CI) / Lift / p-value

understanding.purpose: Compare checkout metrics between control and variant, including estimated lift, uncertainty, and statistical significance.
understanding.reading: Readers scan metric names down the first column, then compare the two means and confidence intervals across each row before checking lift and p-value. Wrapped labels should remain visually connected to their values.
groups: Control and Variant each pair a mean with a 95% confidence interval; matching subcolumns support comparison between the two groups.
Lift and p-value summarize the comparison and should remain easy to scan alongside the group results.
keep_intact: Individual numbers, percentages, currency amounts, time values, and p-values.
Confidence interval ranges where possible, especially time and currency ranges.
Short column headers and metric identifiers such as 7-day and 1,000.
may_wrap: Long metric names at word boundaries, especially Support contacts per 1,000 sessions.
Confidence intervals at natural break points if space is prioritized for metric names; affected rows will become taller.
The two-level Control and Variant headers already occupy two header rows.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Refine r1A by moving 1px from Metric to p-value. This aims to keep the p-value header intact while preserving one-line confidence intervals.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Use closely matched widths for Control and Variant and generous summary columns, with a narrow metric column and nearly full-width confidence intervals.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Give one more pixel to metric labels while preserving the interval, mean, and lift widths that work in r0A. Check whether the p-value header still fits at 68px; r0B shows that this width is close to its wrapping threshold.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give metric names more room while keeping means, lift, and p-values at r0A widths. The narrower interval columns will wrap some ranges, so compare the resulting row rhythm and readability against r0A.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give Metric more room than in r1A while retaining matched proportions between the Control and Variant subcolumns. This tests whether some label wrapping can be reduced with less disruption to confidence intervals than in r1B.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Give Metric 5px more than r2A while retaining most of the interval width. This tests whether a label can wrap more naturally without introducing as much interval wrapping as r2B.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Test a wider Metric column to improve label scanning, accepting that the longest confidence intervals will wrap. Keep corresponding Control and Variant columns close in width.

bad.name: r0B
bad.note: Give metric names more room while accepting wraps in the longest confidence intervals.
bad.why: The p-value header wraps, and several lift values split the percent sign from the number. Time values also wrap, disrupting comparisons across the row.

rationale: r2A keeps both confidence intervals, means, lift values, and p-values on one line, making the control and variant results easy to compare across each row. Several metric names wrap naturally, but the shaded row-header column keeps them identifiable and the two-level header remains clear. The modest increase in height preserves the integrity of the numerical results.

general: Give paired columns enough similar space to support comparison, while allowing for differences in their content.
Protect numerical values and units from disruptive breaks; natural wrapping in descriptive labels can be a reasonable tradeoff.
Judge row height alongside readability and grouping rather than treating compactness as the goal.
specific: The confidence intervals need substantially more width than the means, especially for checkout time.
A narrow p-value column wraps its hyphenated header, and a narrow lift column separates percent signs from values.

tradeoffs: r3A is shorter and keeps the monetary intervals on one line, but wraps both time intervals. r1B and r3B give metric names more room at the cost of wrapping both monetary and time intervals.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative visual estimates, not independently rendered thresholds. They assume small compensating adjustments to the other columns to stay within 673px; their endpoints should not be combined arbitrarily. A designer who prioritizes scanning metric names or table height may reasonably prefer r3A or r3B.

critique.good: The grouped headers are clear, and matching mean and interval columns make the two versions easy to compare. Numbers, intervals, lift values, and p-values remain intact. Wrapped metric labels stay within their rows.
critique.problems: Five metric labels wrap, producing a relatively tall table and making the first column feel crowded. The short final line of several labels interrupts the scanning rhythm.
critique.cause: The 166px metric column leaves 145px for text. Most remaining width is needed to keep the confidence intervals and other values on one line.

critique.good: The wider metric column keeps most labels on one line and makes the row names easier to scan.
critique.problems: The p-value header wraps, time values and interval ranges break across lines, and several lift percentages split before the percent sign. These breaks scatter related information and make comparisons harder despite the shorter table.
critique.cause: The 100px confidence interval columns are too narrow for the longest ranges; the 65px and 64px mean columns cannot hold the full time values; and the 66px lift and 68px p-value columns are too narrow for their longest contents or header.

critique.good: The mirrored Control and Variant widths create a clear, balanced grouping. Most numeric values remain intact, and the headers are easy to read.
critique.problems: The narrow metric column wraps six labels, including the otherwise short Average order value, making the table tall and the row names harder to scan. The control time interval also wraps, so the matching interval columns do not actually behave alike.
critique.cause: The 140px metric column leaves only 119px for labels. Both interval columns are 120px, but the longest control interval needs approximately 121px including padding; extra width is instead assigned to lift and p-value.

critique.good: Both confidence intervals stay on one line, making the Control and Variant estimates easy to compare. Numerical values remain intact, and wrapped metric labels stay within their rows.
critique.problems: Several metric labels wrap, giving the first column a dense, uneven rhythm. The p-value header also breaks across two lines, weakening an otherwise clear header hierarchy.
critique.cause: The 167px metric column is too narrow for several labels, while the 68px p-value column is just too narrow for its header. The wide confidence interval columns preserve ranges at the expense of label space.

critique.good: The wider metric column keeps more labels on one line, and all headers stay intact. Control and Variant retain parallel proportions, supporting comparison.
critique.problems: Currency and time confidence intervals break across lines in both groups. The separated endpoints make those ranges harder to read and compare, and the taller rows interrupt the otherwise compact rhythm.
critique.cause: The 110px and 107px confidence interval columns do not provide enough text width for the longest ranges. Their space was reassigned chiefly to the 188px metric column.

critique.good: The Control and Variant pairs have similar proportions, and all confidence intervals remain on one line. Numbers are easy to compare across each row, and no words or identifiers split mid-word.
critique.problems: Five metric labels wrap, including checkout completion, cart abandonment, and 7-day repeat purchase. The labels remain legible, but the repeated two-line rows give the table a somewhat uneven rhythm.
critique.cause: The 166px Metric column leaves 145px for text. The 121px and 118px confidence interval columns preserve complete ranges, leaving limited width for longer labels.

critique.good: The 178px Metric column keeps cart abandonment on one line. Headers remain clear, and matching Mean and confidence interval columns retain a coherent grouped structure.
critique.problems: Both currency ranges and both time ranges wrap, separating their endpoints and making those comparisons harder to scan. The extra height in the average order value row offsets the space saved in the cart abandonment row.
critique.cause: The 115px Control interval column and 112px Variant interval column leave too little text width for the longest currency and time ranges. The 12px gained by Metric comes from those interval columns.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0B.why: The wide metric column leaves too little room for results: time values and confidence intervals wrap, several lift values separate from their percent signs, and the p-value header breaks.

r2A.why: All numerical results and headers stay intact. Metric labels wrap naturally, while the control and variant groups have balanced, comparable widths.

ref_auto.why: Most metric labels stay on one line, but both time means and several confidence intervals wrap, as does the p-value header. Lift values remain intact.

ref_equal.why: The metric column is so narrow that labels become tall and 'abandonment' breaks within the word. Several confidence intervals also wrap, while other numeric columns have excess space.

r0C.why: Labels wrap at word boundaries and nearly all results stay intact. The control time confidence interval wraps, making that comparison less immediate.

r1A.why: Numerical results stay intact and the two test groups are balanced, but the p-value header wraps despite the very similar B keeping it on one line.

raw.unsure: The visual distinction between B and F is small; B's intact p-value header makes it preferable.

r0C.why: The grouped columns are balanced and most values stay intact, but the narrow metric column wraps many labels and the control time interval splits across lines.

r2A.why: Metric labels wrap at sensible word boundaries while means, confidence intervals, lifts and p-values stay intact. The matching control and variant groups are easy to compare.

r0B.why: The wider metric column keeps most labels on one line, but time values and currency intervals break across lines, several lifts separate from their percent signs, and the p-value header wraps.

ref_auto.why: Most metric labels and all lifts stay intact, but currency intervals and time values split across lines, and the p-value header wraps.

r1A.why: Labels wrap naturally and all data values remain intact, with balanced control and variant groups. The p-value header wraps unnecessarily.

ref_equal.why: The metric column is so narrow that labels occupy several lines and 'abandonment' breaks within the word. Currency and time intervals also wrap, while short numeric columns have surplus space.

raw.unsure: B and E are close; B has the advantage of keeping the p-value header on one line.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
